Inspect how derived covariates were made

Source: R/landmark_covariates.R
landmark_covariates.Rd

landmark_covariates() returns one row per covariate added by add_landmark_covariates(), with the method and options used and how complete it is in the current rows.

landmark_lme_fits() returns one row per mixed model (each lme variable at each landmark), with fit status, sample sizes, variance components and the fitted lme4::lmer() object in the model column.

Only covariates still present in x are included, so columns removed with dplyr::select() drop out.

Usage

landmark_covariates(x)

landmark_lme_fits(x)

Arguments

x

A landmark_tbl returned by add_landmark_covariates().

Value

landmark_covariates(): a tibble with columns column, source, method, include_at_landmark, lookback, random_slope, adjust, n_rows, n_missing, and, for LOCF, median_lag and max_lag (time between each carried-forward measurement and its landmark). Counts and lags are computed on the current rows, so they follow dplyr::filter().

landmark_lme_fits(): a tibble with columns column, source, .landmark, status ("ok", "warning" or "failed"), message, n_eligible, n_subjects, n_obs, median_obs, time_min, time_max, time_scale, slope (per original time unit), var_intercept, var_slope, var_residual, singular and model (NULL for failed fits). In each model, time (.t) is centred at the landmark and divided by time_scale.

Both return a zero-row tibble with the same columns when there is nothing to report.

See also

add_landmark_covariates()

Examples

visits_pbc <- transform(pbcseq_visits, log_bili = log(bili))
pbc_lm <- pbcseq_baseline |>
  landmark_data(id, futime, status, landmarks = c(365, 730), horizon = 1825) |>
  add_landmark_covariates(
    visits_pbc, id, day,
    locf = albumin, lme = log_bili, lme_args = list(adjust = ~ age)
  )
#> ℹ Ignored 32 rows of `longitudinal_data` whose `id` is not in `landmark_data`.

landmark_covariates(pbc_lm)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   column   source method include_at_landmark lookback random_slope adjust n_rows
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>  <lgl>                  <dbl> <lgl>        <chr>   <int>
#> 1 albumin  album… locf   TRUE                      NA NA           NA        568
#> 2 log_bili log_b… lme    TRUE                      NA FALSE        ~age      568
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_missing <int>, median_lag <dbl>, max_lag <dbl>

fits <- landmark_lme_fits(pbc_lm)
fits
#> # A tibble: 2 × 18
#>   column  source .landmark status message n_eligible n_subjects n_obs median_obs
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <chr>  <chr>        <int>      <int> <int>      <dbl>
#> 1 log_bi… log_b…       365 ok     NA             290        290   642          2
#> 2 log_bi… log_b…       730 ok     NA             278        278   845          3
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: time_min <dbl>, time_max <dbl>, time_scale <dbl>,
#> #   slope <dbl>, var_intercept <dbl>, var_slope <dbl>, var_residual <dbl>,
#> #   singular <lgl>, model <list>
summary(fits$model[[1]])
#> Linear mixed model fit by REML ['lmerMod']
#> Formula: .value ~ .t + age + (1 | .id)
#>    Data: data
#> Control: control
#> 
#> REML criterion at convergence: 1304.3
#> 
#> Scaled residuals: 
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -3.8287 -0.4163  0.0110  0.3826  3.5283 
#> 
#> Random effects:
#>  Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.
#>  .id      (Intercept) 0.8505   0.9222  
#>  Residual             0.1277   0.3574  
#> Number of obs: 642, groups:  .id, 290
#> 
#> Fixed effects:
#>              Estimate Std. Error t value
#> (Intercept)  0.702170   0.272507   2.577
#> .t          -0.007086   0.015214  -0.466
#> age         -0.005363   0.005360  -1.000
